call_chain_analysis: The buns package is a client-side framework whose public API is attached to `buns` and re-exported at the bottom of lib/index.js via `for(var methods in buns) { exports[methods] = buns[methods]; }` (lines 923-925). But reaching the Prototype Pollution sink does NOT go through any exported method: the vulnerability executes at module *top-level* during `require()`. Between lines 151 and 237 the module assigns ten properties onto String.prototype at the global scope (`String.prototype.matchIn = function(regexes){...}` at line 151, then `matchAtLeast` at 164, `matchAtMost` at 180, `matchAll` at 192, `adjustPath` at 208, `splice` at 212, `escape` at 216, `slugify` at 220, `capitalize` at 229, `camelCaseToDash` at 233, `dashToCamelCase` at 237). Each assignment mutates the global `String.prototype`, which is observable in every subsequent script running in the same Node process. Entry point for the harness is therefore the simplest possible one: `require("/work/target/lib/index.js")`. There are no preconditions beyond requiring the module itself: no `buns.json` on disk is needed (the top-level config load at line 55 catches ENOENT and sets `configExists=false`, but the prototype assignments at 151+ do not read `configExists`), no constructor arguments, no exported method call. Jazzer.js's Prototype Pollution bug detector (@jazzer.js/bug-detectors) compares the current String.prototype against a clean baseline and reports every extra property on it, so the detector fires on the very first fuzz iteration — even on an empty byte input — purely because the harness loads the module.
argument_reasoning: The fuzz-controlled byte string is almost irrelevant here: the sink executes once at `require` time, before any fuzzer-shaped input flows through `module.exports.fuzz`. We still consume the full input with `provider.consumeRemainingAsString()` and pipe it through `buns.install(name)` for two reasons: (1) it keeps the harness useful if the fuzzer ever evolves it into a chain where a target-controlled key is written to a prototype in response to input (so the detector would still fire on the richer path), and (2) `install` is the clearest downstream user of fuzz-controlled input in the module and gives the fuzzer something to explore while the detector completes its baseline comparison. We strip NUL bytes with `.replace(/\u0000/g, "")` because Node's `child_process.execSync` rejects strings containing NUL with a `TypeError` — that TypeError is not the bug we want to surface, and letting it escape the fuzz target would end the campaign before the Prototype Pollution detector reports.

lessons: The 7B v4 model marked this as loaded_not_reached, which suggests the model is anchoring on an exported-method sink (it looks at the public API surface and tries to drive input THROUGH a function) and does not notice that pollution happens at module top-level, before any fuzz_fn invocation. Three things the model probably missed: (1) `String.prototype.X = ...` written at module scope is itself the sink — the exploit is `require(target)` and nothing else, so a FuzzedDataProvider body is irrelevant to confirmation; (2) Jazzer.js's Prototype Pollution detector compares against a clean baseline and reports differences on every iteration, so an empty-input crash is a legitimate confirmed crash and should not be filtered out as a 'degenerate' run by the model's post-processor; (3) when the SAST class is prototype-pollution, scan the full file for top-level `*.prototype.*=` writes before planning a call chain — that search would have taken this case from loaded_not_reached to confirmed in one attempt.
